Hey Everyone 👋 I live in the terminal. I write code in Neovim and use lazygit, lazydocker and other TUIs every day. But each time I had to work with AWS, I had to leave the terminal for the console or type long CLI commands just to answer simple questions. Which instances are running? What is in this bucket? Did that Lambda deploy? I wanted the lazygit feel for AWS too, so I built my own: Lazy AWS. What it does: - Browse EC2, ECS, ECR, S3 and Lambda in one terminal UI - Filter lists, see related resources and read the full JSON details - Run actions such as stopping an instance or uploading a file, always with a confirmation step Try it in 10 seconds: $ brew install capybara-brain346/tap/lazyaws $ lazyaws

# Your cloud. Your terminal.

Meet Lazy AWS. A keyboard-driven home for your AWS resources.  
 Browse, inspect, and act. Without the console shuffle.

Get started Take a quick tour

lazyaws — demo

Real Lazy AWS EC2 demo. Resource lists appear beside the selected resource’s JSON details.

Real interface. Sample resources.Made for your keyboard.

## Less setup. More getting things done.

We support macOS, Ubuntu, Arch Linux, and Omarchy. Windows is not supported.

Before you startAWS CLI v2

Choose curl or Homebrew to install on macOS or Linux. Then run the demo or connect your AWS account. Debian installs are available without a support guarantee. AWS CLI v2 and credentials are needed only for your AWS account.

1. 1

   ### Install with curl [...] That’s the short version.Explore the service guide [...] 1. 1

   ### Install with curl

   Install the binary to ~/.local/bin. Add this directory to your PATH if needed.

   terminal

   ```
   curl -fsSL  | sh
   ```
2. 2

   ### Or install with Homebrew

   Install from our tap on macOS or Linux with Homebrew.

   terminal

   ```
   brew install capybara-brain346/tap/lazyaws
   ```
3. 3

   ### Run the installed demo

   Start with local sample data. No AWS account or credentials needed.

   terminal

   ```
   lazyaws --demo
   ```
4. 4

   ### Connect your account

   Use an existing AWS CLI profile. Sign in first if your profile uses SSO.

   terminal

   ```
   aws sso login --profile dev lazyaws --profile dev --region eu-west-1
   ```

## A small learning curve. A lot less clicking.

Three stops. Then you know your way around.

results.title: GitHub - fuziontech/lazyaws: Terminal UI for managing AWS resources, inspired by lazygit, k9s, and lazydocker · GitHub
results.content:
### Navigation

 VIM-style keybindings - j/k, g/G, Ctrl+d/u for navigation
 Search - `/` to search, `n/N` for next/prev match
 Commands - `:q` quit, `:r` refresh, `:help` show help, `:ec2/:s3/:eks` switch services
 Multi-region/account - `:region` and `:account` to switch contexts

## Installation

```
cd
```

## Usage

```
lazyaws
```

Press `:help` or `?` for keyboard shortcuts.

### Quick Start

Connect to EC2 via SSM:

1. Press `/` to search for instance
2. Press `c` to connect
3. Ctrl+C works inside session (kills commands, not the session)
4. `exit` to return to lazyaws

Edit S3 file:

1. Navigate to object
2. Press `e` to edit in $EDITOR
3. Save and quit
4. File automatically uploads
5. Returns to same S3 location

Key Shortcuts: [...] Key Shortcuts:

```
j/k, ↑/↓ Navigate g/G Top/bottom Ctrl+d/u Page down/up / Search n/N Next/prev match Enter Select/view details Esc/q Back/quit :help Show help 
```

EC2:

```
s/S Start/stop r/t Reboot/terminate c SSM connect 9 Launch k9s (EKS nodes) Space Multi-select 
```

S3:

```
e Edit file in $EDITOR d Download D Delete (typed confirmation) u Presigned URL p/v Policy/versioning 
```

EKS:

```
9 Launch k9s u Update kubeconfig 
```

## Configuration

Uses existing AWS CLI configuration (`~/.aws/config` and `~/.aws/credentials`).

```
# Set up credentials # export # Use specific profile # export # Override region #
```

### SSO Authentication

lazyaws supports AWS SSO with automatic account and region selection. [...] ## Features

### EC2

 List instances with color-coded states
 Start/stop/reboot/terminate instances
 Multi-select for bulk operations
 SSM sessions with proper Ctrl+C handling
 View instance details, metrics, and health checks
 k9s integration for EKS nodes
 Returns to EC2 view after SSM exit

### S3

 Browse buckets and objects
 Edit files in $EDITOR - press `e` to edit, auto-uploads on save
 Download/delete objects with typed confirmation
 Generate presigned URLs
 View bucket policies and versioning
 Returns to same location after editing

### EKS

 List clusters with status
 View node groups and add-ons
 Update kubeconfig automatically
 Launch k9s for clusters
